clue.text: Cut down on work but somehow got in, of course

indicators.note: done somehow means done in no particular way, so the word but arrives jumbled
getting in means slipping inside something else, so the jumbled word sits within the other pieces

blocks.note: to do is to work
taken as written, then rearranged
cut down, as an adjective, means reduced: less

explanation.surface: Someone trimmed their working hours yet still managed to get in somewhere, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' is not a verb here but an adjective meaning reduced; 'on' means placed after, as it often does in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are sentence adverbs expressing certainty, used to say something is surely or naturally so.

clue.text: Extremely deceptive title, but one clears screen film

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the two ends of the word
Mister is a title of address

explanation.surface: A misleading film title, alongside someone clearing a cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screen film' suggests a movie, but it is the misty film on a car's windscreen.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's heater device that removes condensation from the windscreen glass is called a demister in Britain.

clue.text: Source of milk shake? Not initial-ly

indicators.note: not initially tells you the opening letters are missing, dropped from the front

blocks.note: to shudder is to shake

explanation.surface: A milk shake, oddly qualified as not being the original kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The split 'initial-ly' hints that more than one opening letter goes: SH comes off the front of the shake.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's mammary gland is the organ from which dairy farmers draw their product.

clue.text: Catch the swine pinching new harness

indicators.note: pinching means grabbing hold, so the swine word holds the next letter inside it

blocks.note: to trap is to catch
swine are pigs
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Trapping pigs that have stolen a new set of tack.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the ornamental harness and coverings of a horse, the original sense before 'outward signs'.

clue.text: Confirm death - animal has been beheaded

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, so the animal loses its first letter

blocks.note: death is the end
a horse is an animal

explanation.surface: Certifying that an animal died by decapitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse something is to give approval or ratify it, as when backing a decision formally.

clue.text: Know-all explains why theatre's closed

definitions.note: read as the phrase SHOW OFF, a show cancelled

blocks.note: first meaning: a boastful person who flaunts what they know
second meaning: the show is off, so the doors stay shut

explanation.surface: A smart alec gives his reasons for the theatre shutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a boastful person, and the noun naming someone who parades their abilities fits that type.

clue.text: Pierced one's skin

blocks.note: to pierce is to cut
one is I, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: Someone has had a piercing through the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical Latin term for the true skin, the dermis and outer layer together.

clue.text: Original American line accepted there may be a catch in it

definitions.text: there may be a catch in it

indicators.note: accepted means taken on board, so the tribe name takes on the next letter

blocks.note: the Cree are a Native American people
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An authentic US contract line has been agreed, though it may hide a snag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catch' sounds like a hidden snag, but it is an angler's haul of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which anglers carry the fish they have landed.

clue.text: Borrow, say, from one who may have some cheques

definitions.text: one who may have some cheques

blocks.note: first meaning: George Borrow, the Victorian author who wandered Spain and England

blocks.clueFragment: one who may have some cheques
blocks.note: second meaning: a holder of ... cheques

explanation.surface: Taking out a loan from someone with a chequebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' looks like a verb but is George Borrow, the 19th-century writer of travel books such as The Bible in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrow is an example of a famous wanderer, and holiday-makers once carried special cheques bearing that name.

clue.text: Classic sea hazard that is capsizing mate

indicators.note: a capsizing boat turns upside down, so in this down entry the pieces read upwards

blocks.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means that is to say
an ally is a mate

explanation.surface: A legendary sea danger that turns over your shipmate.
explanation.walkthrough: SC for scilicet is less familiar than IE for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the monster Scylla, facing the whirlpool Charybdis, menaced sailors in a strait.

clue.text: Communication channels in Iran's territory once

blocks.note: first meaning: press, radio and television
second meaning: the ancient land of the Medes in what is now north-west Iran

explanation.surface: A report on the broadcasting networks operating in Iran in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of medium names mass communication outlets, and the same word is the classical kingdom of the Medes.

clue.text: This roamed all over the place in desert conditions

definitions.text: This roamed all over the place in desert conditions

indicators.note: scattered all over the place, the letters of roamed lose their order
in places the jumbled letters inside the word for desert conditions

blocks.note: deserts are dry; this word wraps around the rest
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: This creature wandered everywhere across arid desert land.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'This' is the beast, and the rest both describes it and builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-humped Arabian camel is the classic animal that wanders across dry sandy wastes.

clue.text: Fighter with power halved is cleaner

indicators.note: cut in half, the pair of power letters keeps only one of the two

blocks.note: a scrapper is someone who fights
P is the abbreviation for power; the fighter contains two of them

explanation.surface: A boxer whose strength has been cut in half turns into a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: The fighter's PP is the 'power' that gets halved, leaving one P.
explanation.definitionFit: A scraper is a hand tool used to clean mud, paint or residue off a surface.

clue.text: Whence flows prosperity after a strike?

definitions.text: Whence flows prosperity after a strike?

blocks.clueFragment: Whence flows prosperity after a strike?
blocks.note: surface reading: what brings wealth back once industrial action ends
setter's reading: striking oil, a gusher that pours out riches

explanation.walkthrough: A strike suggests workers walking out, but here it is a drilling strike, the moment oil is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore that taps crude petroleum produces money once drillers have hit a reservoir.

clue.text: Relatively large group?

blocks.note: surface reading: a group that is fairly big
setter's reading: a group of relatives, a large clan of kin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean 'fairly', but it means 'in terms of relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a big kin network including aunts, uncles, cousins and grandparents beyond parents and children.

clue.text: Fundamentally change exercises one's left speechless

indicators.note: having left means having gone away, so that letter departs from the exercises word

blocks.note: to train is to exercise
I is the Roman numeral one
mute means unable to speak

explanation.surface: Physical exercise has changed someone so much it left them lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's left' reads as 'one has left', the I departing.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmute is to alter the nature or substance of something, as alchemists hoped with base metal.

clue.text: Where New Testament may be briefly read in Christmas season?

definitions.text: Where New Testament may be briefly
definitions.note: a cryptic locator: in the middle of the season's name

blocks.clueFragment: Where New Testament may be briefly
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: the abbreviated Testament sits in the middle of the cold season's name
second meaning: the depth of the cold months around the solstice

explanation.surface: Where in the festive season a congregation might hear a short Gospel reading.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the short form of New Testament, and it sits right in the middle of WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive December period falls near the solstice, the depth of the cold months.

clue.text: Invite trouble, like Oliver Twist wanting more?

blocks.note: first meaning: behave so as to deserve punishment
second meaning: literally request it, as Oliver asked for more gruel

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist, in Dickens, provoked fury by holding out his bowl for more.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to provoke one's own punishment, and literally it describes making a request.

clue.text: Prepare to fight to make improvements

blocks.note: first meaning: hoist the battle flags of an army
second meaning: lift the level of quality

explanation.surface: Getting ready for battle in order to make things better.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards are both military banners hoisted before battle and levels of quality that can be lifted.

clue.text: Took action about learners - one produced bad marks

indicators.note: about means around, so the action word goes around the others

blocks.note: to sue is to take legal action
L is a learner driver's plate, doubled for the plural
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone took action over students after one of them got poor grades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad marks' sounds like poor grades, but means stains.
explanation.definitionFit: To sully is to soil or stain, so the past tense means left dirty smudges or blemishes.

clue.text: A noble Roman moving right up tree

indicators.note: moving takes that letter out of its place in the Roman's name so it can go higher

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
Brutus, the aristocratic conspirator against Caesar

explanation.surface: A patrician Roman shins up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means earlier: the R leaves BRUTUS and climbs to just after A.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus is the strawberry tree, an evergreen with red berries in the heather family.

clue.text: Raised large stake as place for execution

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means read bottom to top

blocks.note: big means large
a stake is a bet

explanation.surface: A tall post put up for an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stake' suggests a post for burning, but it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is a gallows, an upright post with an arm from which hanged criminals were displayed.

clue.text: Establish where cattle may be?

definitions.note: read as the phrase IN STALL

blocks.note: first meaning: set up or put in place
second meaning: in a stall, a compartment in a cowshed

explanation.surface: Working out where the herd might be housed.
explanation.definitionFit: To install someone or something is to settle it in position; split, the word places beasts in their shed compartment.

clue.text: Like a fruit? Put in request

blocks.note: first meaning: apple-like, a whimsical adjective
second meaning: submit a formal application

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey reading of the word as tasting of a common orchard fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply is to make a formal request, and the playful reading suggests having the quality of an orchard pome.

clue.text: He may get a punch, having trouble gaining entry

definitions.text: He may get a punch, having trouble gaining entry

indicators.note: something gaining entry gets inside, so the trouble word goes into the punch word

blocks.note: a biff is a blow with the fist
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: An officer forcing his way into a house may be thumped for his pains.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and builds it: a bailiff is the court officer who enters homes to seize goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A court officer who serves writs and seizes debtors' property often meets hostility at the door.

clue.text: I struggled to get into such an elite college?

blocks.note: taken as written
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A student fought hard to win a place at a top university.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy League colleges in the US are the elite ones; their old buildings are covered in climbing ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied means overgrown with climbing creeper, the image behind the prestigious Ivy League universities.

clue.text: Plan of Berlin put out

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or upset, so the letters leave their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scheme for Berlin has been issued or published.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed technical drawing, and so any design or scheme for doing something.

clue.text: Persistent type of judge?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who keeps trying
second meaning: one who tries a case

explanation.surface: Asking whether a judge is a dogged sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one who keeps making efforts and one who hears and decides a legal case.

clue.text: Minute appears years to adolescent

indicators.note: to here means added on to, so one piece is joined to the end of another

blocks.note: a teen is an adolescent
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: Time seems to pass like years for a teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like a unit of time; it is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means extremely small, which is what teeny means informally.

clue.text: Doubt one's tried to smash earlier record

indicators.note: to smash something is to break it into fragments that can be put together differently

blocks.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
taken as written
a CD is a compact disc, a recording format

explanation.surface: Questioning whether an athlete really attempted to beat a previous record.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to refuse belief in it or cast suspicion on it.
